bad.title: Limited Use of Iterative Testing and Refinement
bad.description: You tend to develop solutions independently and present them as complete products rather than engaging in progressive testing cycles. This means you often miss opportunities to validate assumptions early, discover gaps through experimentation, and strengthen your approaches through multiple rounds of feedback and adjustment.

bad.title: Underutilization of AI as a Thinking Partner
bad.description: Your workflow relies heavily on your own analysis rather than actively engaging AI to explore uncertainties, test hypotheses, or examine alternative perspectives. This independent approach limits your ability to leverage AI's strengths in generating possibilities, challenging your reasoning, and helping you discover insights you might not reach alone.

bad.title: Incomplete Mental Models in Task Design
bad.description: While you establish solid conceptual frameworks, you sometimes omit the concrete examples, edge cases, and comprehensive guidance that would make your instructions reliably actionable across diverse scenarios. This can leave gaps that reduce AI performance quality in situations beyond the most straightforward applications.

good.title: Evidence-Based Verification and Quality Control
good.description: You consistently anchor your evaluations in concrete evidence—providing specific citations, timestamps, and corpus references to validate information. This disciplined approach to verification creates a reliable foundation for decision-making and demonstrates strong commitment to accuracy over assumption.

good.title: Clear Articulation of Complex Distinctions
good.description: You excel at translating abstract concepts into precise language that captures subtle but important differences. Whether distinguishing between subjective and objective measurement or explaining conceptual categories, you communicate nuanced ideas with clarity that both humans and AI systems can understand and act upon.

good.title: Strategic Prioritization of Meaningful Issues
good.description: You demonstrate sound judgment in separating substantive problems from trivial variations, focusing your attention on issues that genuinely matter. This ability to filter noise and identify what deserves deeper examination allows you to work efficiently through complex materials without getting lost in unimportant details.

overall.overview: Throughout this assessment, you demonstrated **strong analytical foundations and methodical verification practices** that enable you to work efficiently and produce quality results. Your ability to **identify meaningful patterns, articulate precise distinctions, and ground your evaluations in concrete evidence** reflects solid collaborative capability. The primary opportunity for growth lies in **shifting from independent problem-solving toward iterative AI collaboration**—actively using dialogue to test hypotheses, refine your approaches, and explore uncertainties would unlock deeper insights and more robust outcomes.

improvements.title: Adopt a Test-First Approach to Validate Your Designs
improvements.description: Before finalizing any prompt, instruction set, or analytical framework, test it with AI using diverse scenarios—including edge cases and challenging examples. Treat each test as a learning opportunity that reveals where your design needs refinement, then iterate based on what you discover. This cycle of testing and adjustment will significantly improve the reliability and robustness of your work.

improvements.title: Use AI Dialogue to Explore Uncertainties Actively
improvements.description: When you encounter ambiguity or complexity, engage AI in exploratory conversation rather than working through problems entirely on your own. Pose hypotheses and ask AI to help you test them, request alternative interpretations of evidence, and use the dialogue to surface assumptions you might not have considered. This collaborative exploration will deepen your insights and reveal dimensions of problems you might otherwise miss.

improvements.title: Build Complete Mental Models with Examples and Edge Cases
improvements.description: When designing prompts or instructions, go beyond high-level principles to include concrete examples that illustrate your intent, boundary conditions that define limits, and edge cases that test understanding. This richer context helps AI grasp not just what you want, but why—creating more robust and reliable performance across the full range of situations you'll encounter.
